comment: He is very knowledgeable about the material and very down-to-earth. Very straightforward grading and class structure. Mostly discussions and readings for homework. Low pressure class

Dr. Winiarski is a really great professor who really cares about his students and the subjects he teaches. As long as you participate and put in some effort, you will get an A. And Dr. Winiarski wants you to get an A, so he will help and guide you with whatever you need. He is a 10/10 professor who I recommend everyone should take.

love prof winiarski! took this to fulfill a gen ed and it was super easy and very engaging even though the topics weren't really stuff i would normally care about. amount of homework varies but it's very reading heavy so be prepared to read! no tests but 3 one paragraph essays (u can revise) and one full final paper! would totally recommend
Such an amazing and passionate professor. Sex & Salvation was a great class, and I would definitely take Dr. Winiarski again.
Dr. Winikarski is a great professor, and this was an easy A course, but I did learn a lot even though it was not difficult
This guy was great! Made me feel like I was respected. Class wasn't hard, but it had a lot of reading. He really cared about making us better writers! Funny Guy!

He is nice and knowledgeble about the subject, but there is a lot of reading to do. IMO too much for an FYS. Also he demands a lot of participation. The final paper is disproportionately difficult compared to what we did during the semester. But in general the class is not hard.

Dr. Winiarski is a really good professor. He gave good feedback on writing assignments and understands that not everyone is super into the material. I would recommend taking this FYS. It's very low key compared to other FYS classes with 3 OPAs, a presentation, and a final paper. He also does contract grading which is really nice.

Dr. Winiarski is a really good professor who cares a lot about teaching and is realistic about it. He is a really smart and interesting guy, and you actually learn something without too much effort. He understands that he is teaching an FYS course and not a 300-level class, so he sets standards, but he keeps everything very attainable.

I think Dr Winiarski is a great professor, and he teaches the material very clearly. I recommend taking this class because of his unique style of grading, which made it very easy to do well in the class while putting in minimum effort. Material can be a bit boring, but if you are looking for an easy FYS class then I definitely recommend this class.

The class is not hard but I think he sometimes forgets that this topic of "microhistory" is something we are literally just now hearing about. For some of the assignments, it felt like he didn't really prepare us enough, especially this final paper. As a person though, he's not bad it's just the class itself, mostly if religion doesn't interest you

Doug is clearly very accomplished in his field, but if you're not into witchcraft and religious cults, this class is excruciating. You have to dedicate tons of time outside of class to do well, which is difficult if you're not into the material. Bit of a strange guy, but I'm sure he's a great teacher if you're into what he's into.
Dr. Winiarski truly cares about his students and wants to instill his love of history within them. The homework mainly consists of reading and there are a few essays. Take this class for FYS!

He is an awesome professor! You will take a lot away from his lectures. Also, he is very willing to help students outside of class and will make sure you understand the material. Get ready to work though, you can not get around his class by not participating or reading the material he assigns.
Great Professor. Hard grader and can be tough but overall very knowledgeable.

Dr. Winiarski is extremely knowledgeable and invested in what we do in class which makes it super engaging to maintain discussions. He is super nice and can meet pretty much anytime and really developed my reading analysis skills. You get a lot out of the class despite not having a ton of reading. He gives us a lot of his own expertise.

Dr. Winiarski is a very knowledgeable professor. Though his class is essay-heavy, he is super accessible and willing to give you a zoom call whenever you need help with the assignments. Getting an A is pretty much achievable but he makes sure you have to work for it. Came out of the class as a better writer, would recommend for FHST.

Devil in the Details: had the potential to be really interesting, it was not. Main criticisms was the amount of HW. A lot of readings and didn't feel the need to put much effort into them because he would go over the entire reading in class so felt like the HW was useless. Very accessible and helpful outside of class, but not the best class

Dr. Winiarski is an awesome professor who really loves what he teaches. He is super smart and does not do well to hide his pride. The coursework can be really heavy (he expects a ton) and sometimes it feels like he evaluates students differently. Ask him how you could improve your assignments, he doesn't provide much feedback without your request.

Professor Winiarski is a very knowledgeable professor that knows what he's talking about and knows how to teach. However, this class is only essays and participation so if you don't excel with essays, probably not the class for you.

Professor Winiarksi is the best professor I have ever had. You will not be able to look away when he is talking. His lectures are not often but I always looked forward to them because of how good he is at teaching and keeping students interested. Super helpful and committed to his students. I signed up to take another one of his classes!

AMAZING! One of my favorite professors I've had a UR for Devil in the Details. He is so clear with grading criteria, assignments, and classroom topics. It's also such an interesting course--unlike anything else you'll take at UR. Participation is huge. Because of him, I'm thinking of minoring in Religious Studies (and I'm not religious at all).
Great Professor. He's very engaged and enthusiastic about teaching.

Dr. Winiarski is an amazing and very intelligent professor. I took the FYS American Gods, and although the first third of the course was a bit dry, the majority of the course and the readings were so interesting. Participation and papers make your grade.
Participation is basically everything. No tests. Papers are very important, but he gives a lot of help if you ask for it. Overall very good professor!

Dr. Winiarski is very passionate about Native American studies (perhaps too passionate?) The class is usually interesting but can get a little dry. The readings are the worst part; they're beyond boring. Additionally, you will use all of your printer credits printing the articles out. Very hard essay grader. Participation is huge for a good grade

Dr Winiarski is the man I've had him for multiple classes because I love the way he teaches and grading style. He is so clear with expectations and assignments and he is so smart. He will always help you, def go to his office hours. Theres always a massive final paper but he is fair with grading. participate in class, there is also lot of reading

Courses for this class are ridiculously hard, especially for a level 200 class. I do not recommend taking this class for your history requirement unless you intend on being a religion major. You learn a lot of interesting stuff, but he's just an impossible grader. I'm lucky to be getting by with a B as it is.

Native American Religions- He takes this 200 level class way too seriously. He is an interesting professor but the paper assignments are very difficult and he grades them hard. Attendance is mandatory and you are "graded" on not just if you participated but how "good" your contributions were.
Extremely intelligent, helpful, flexible, and treats you as an equal.
Great Teacher, sometimes unorganized but he's very flexible with due dates. Interesting material and fun class. Reasonable amounds of work, got harder towards the end. Very nice guy, I learned a lot!
Tough, but I learned more from him that I have learned from any professor oncampus.
dr. w has definitely improved since he started teaching here. tough but fair.
